kits.familyName: Owning a mistake and its consequences
setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, and you have just realized you made a mistake at work.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you notice that something you did earlier caused a problem.
detail: It is late in the afternoon.
pressure: {coworker3} says nobody has noticed, so you can leave it.
You are worried about how this will look.

tiers.1: Fix a hazard you caused before you explain it.
tiers.2: People waiting on your work need early warning when it will be late.
tiers.3: Do not let someone else carry blame for your mistake.
tiers.4: Repair the effect of a mistake on the person it affected.
tiers.5: Changing how you work prevents the next mistake and can follow the urgent fixes.

fact: You forgot to mark a wet floor, and a customer nearly slipped, though nobody was hurt.
issues.action: Put out the warning sign now, then tell {lead|the} what happened.
issues.brief: mark the floor and report the lapse
issues.reason: The hazard is still there, so it is fixed first. Reporting lets {lead|the} stop a repeat.
issues.lesson: If your mistake created a hazard, make it safe first and then report it.

shortcut.text: Mark the floor and say nothing, since no one was hurt.
shortcut.brief: mark the floor and say nothing
shortcut.why: Reporting lets {lead|the} prevent a repeat, and quiet fixes hide a pattern.
shortcut.mis: If nobody is hurt, nothing needs reporting.

clear: A warning sign is already standing on the floor you forgot to mark.

fact: You promised a task by today but started it late, so it will not be finished on time.
issues.short: the task that will be late
issues.action: Tell {lead|the} now, explain what happened, and offer a new time.
issues.brief: tell {lead|the} and offer a new time
issues.reason: Early notice lets others adjust. Silence leaves them depending on work that is not coming.
issues.lesson: If you will miss a deadline, say so early and offer a new time.

shortcut.text: Wait until the deadline passes and hope nobody asks.
shortcut.brief: wait and hope nobody asks about the task
shortcut.why: Others may be counting on the work, and silence takes away their chance to adjust.
shortcut.mis: Silence is better than admitting a late start.

clear: You already told {lead|the} that your late task would miss its deadline, and it was moved.

fact: {coworker} is being blamed for a stock shortage that came from your counting mistake.
issues.action: Tell {lead|the} the miscount was yours and offer to fix the count.
issues.brief: own the miscount and fix it
issues.reason: Staying quiet leaves someone else carrying your mistake. Owning it clears them and fixes the count.
issues.lesson: Own your mistake rather than let someone else take the blame.

shortcut.text: Let it go, since the shortage is already assigned to {coworker}.
shortcut.why: Staying quiet leaves someone else carrying a mistake that was yours.
shortcut.mis: A mistake belongs to whoever is blamed.

clear: {Lead|the} already knows your counting mistake caused the stock shortage.

fact: A customer's order went to the wrong address because of your typo, and a replacement can ship today.
issues.short: the order sent to the wrong address
issues.action: Send the replacement today and tell the customer what went wrong.
issues.reason: A clear explanation with a real fix shows the customer that the mistake is being handled.
issues.lesson: Fix the effect of your mistake on the person it affected, and be clear about what happened.

shortcut.text: Blame the delivery service and wait for the customer to complain.
shortcut.why: The mistake was yours, and waiting leaves the customer without their order.
shortcut.mis: Blaming someone else protects your reputation.

clear: A replacement for the misdirected order already shipped and the customer was told.

fact: You made the same data-entry mistake twice this week, and {lead|the} offered a short checklist to use.
issues.action: Use the checklist and ask {lead|the} to check your next few entries.
issues.brief: use the checklist and ask {lead|the} to check
issues.reason: A specific change in how you work does more than trying harder, and checks show whether it is working.
issues.lesson: Change how you work after a repeated mistake, instead of just promising to be careful.

shortcut.text: Just try to be more careful without changing how you work.
shortcut.brief: just try to be more careful
shortcut.why: Good intentions rarely change a habit without a specific change in method.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations is a mistake or its effect that you need to deal with.
proceed.lesson: Owning a mistake means fixing it, saying so, and changing what caused it.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} whether they would mention it if they were you.
generic.why: Someone else's opinion does not fix the problem or tell the right person.
generic.mis: The right move depends on what others would do.

generic.text: Fix it quietly so nobody has a reason to bring it up.
generic.why: A quiet fix leaves out the people who need to know what happened.
generic.mis: Mistakes are best fixed in private.

overcaution.text: Stop all your work for the day until {lead|the} decides what should happen to you.
overcaution.why: The problem has a specific fix. Stopping everything delays other work.
overcaution.mis: A mistake means stopping all work.

setup: You discover that an order you entered earlier has the wrong quantity.

steps.text: Confirm what the order should say
Correct the quantity in the system
Tell {lead|the} what you found and fixed
Choose one check to prevent a repeat

rel: You need the right number before you correct it.
Your report should say what you fixed.
Understand the mistake before deciding how to prevent a repeat.
process.lesson: Confirm the facts, fix it, tell the right person, then change your method.

title: Notes on owning a mistake
intro: You are reading a coworker's draft advice about handling mistakes.
prompt: Which line gives advice that avoids responsibility?
doc.lesson: Taking responsibility means fixing the problem, telling the right person and changing the cause.

lines.text: If your mistake creates a hazard, make it safe first and then report it.

bad.text: If your mistake creates a hazard, finish your task before dealing with it.
bad.why: A hazard stays dangerous until it is fixed, so it comes first.

lines.text: If you will miss a deadline, tell people early and offer a new time.

bad.text: If you will miss a deadline, wait and see whether anyone asks.
bad.why: Waiting takes away the time others need to adjust.

lines.text: If someone is blamed for your mistake, tell the person in charge.
lines.fine: Keeps blame with the right person.

bad.text: If someone is already blamed for your mistake, leave it so you avoid more trouble.
bad.why: The other person carries the cost of your mistake, which is not fair to them.

lines.text: After a repeated mistake, change how you work, not just how hard you try.

review.notes: Everyday workplace mistakes only. Priorities: hazards, early warning, fairness to others, repair, prevention. No disciplinary or legal consequences are described.
